criterion: data loss on update of a persisted entry
finding: Redefining an existing glossary term deletes the lines under its definition, including the Related/Avoid line.
why: afkv2/GLOSSARY.md uses '**Term**:', the definition, then a '`Related:` ...' line with no blank line between. The pattern (?:.+\n?)* swallows all of those lines and the replacement writes only term and definition. A term written in the inline form '**Term**: text' does not match, so a duplicate entry is appended.
fix: Replace only the definition line(s) and keep any line that starts with '`Related:`' or '`Avoid:`'; match the inline form too.
evidence: pattern = re.compile(rf"^\*\*{re.escape(term)}\*\*:\n(?:.+\n?)*", re.M)

criterion: error and rollback paths: a carried point is judged by one mention
finding: The check that every returning point has a new card counts any mention of the old card id, so a card that only depends on it counts as carrying it.
why: Round 1 leaves debate card i-3 open and unanswered. Round 2 adds a decided card with depends_on ["i-3"] (the 'holds if' case in ROUNDS.md:48). _decided_fields writes 'depends-on: i-3' into its body, so _names_card matches and the build passes. i-3 is never asked again. The gate reads only the current round (grill_log.py:209) and returning() skips an open old card with no note, so the exit gate can pass with i-3 unsettled. The same mention test in _carried (round_document.py:183-186) drops a reopen mark on a settled card when any later-round card lists it. That reopen has no note, so the end point is the own round and any later mention counts.
fix: Count a card as carrying a point only when its body names the id in a dedicated carry field or component, never in depends_on or free text; make _carried compare against the round of the reopen, not the card's own round.
evidence: lost = [item["id"] for item in returned if not any(_names_card(new, item["id"]) for new in new_items)]

criterion: open-question
finding: Step 5 says 'On check, fix the named field', but no command can fix a built round. A second build is refused.
why: build writes the round to the document and appends it as current with no answer. The engine check (props are checked by the engine, not by the builder) can then refuse it, for example a bad table prop. A second build runs _close_current and refuses with round-not-sent, so the agent must hand-edit the JSON document or stop. Unverified: the real engine is not in this tree, and only the fake engine was available.
fix: Let build replace the current round when it has no answer, or run the check on the round input before the document is written.
evidence: if not current.get("responses"): raise Refusal("round-not-sent", ... ) (round_document.py:193-194)

criterion: open-question: most important problem no checklist item covers
finding: On Codex the raw answer reaches `raw_file` only because the model re-types the hook text, so the stored `raw` is not guaranteed to be exact.
why: ADR-0001 and ADR-0002 (requirements) rest on a stored raw response that audits can trust, but this path has no check that the typed text equals the hook text (unverified: the Stop hook is not on this branch, so whether the reason text is the raw response without any wrapper is also unverified).
fix: Ask S1 for a hook or engine path that writes the answer to a file, or ingest from the hook payload, so the model never copies it.
evidence: "Write that text to `raw_file`, word for word." ... SDD §4: "raw is the exact text"

criterion: Acceptance 3 and 4: wait and ingest drive the SDD §3 engine verbs
finding: The calls `show DOC`, `poll DOC`, `ingest DOC --raw-file F` and the poll answer key `raw` come from the grill's own fake, not from a frozen contract.
why: SDD §3 gives only "page document path; ingest also takes the raw response text", and the ADR-0001 sequence shows `show page` and `poll page`, so the real engine may differ (unverified: the engine is not on origin/feat/afkv2-s1).
fix: Pin the argument and answer shapes in a shared contract with S1, or record the guess as a plan decision and re-check when the engine merges.
evidence: `_engine("ingest", doc, "--raw-file", raw_file)`; fake_engine.py line 160 `argv[argv.index("--raw-file") + 1]`; ADR-0001: "K->>E: show page / poll page"

criterion: Acceptance 6 (PRD AC-002): a later session continues from disk alone
finding: Resume picks the open session by file mtime, which a git clone or checkout resets.
why: After a fresh checkout with two grill documents, the picked file may be the passed session, so `_open_session` returns None and the open session is abandoned for a new one.
fix: Order by `session.started` and id, as `_session_documents` already does, or use the timestamp in the file name.
evidence: documents = sorted(pages.glob("grill-*.json"), key=lambda path: path.stat().st_mtime)

criterion: Acceptance 2: page document `pages/grill-<session id>.json` in the spec folder
finding: The skill puts the folder at `<config spec_folder>/<ticket slug>/`, but no PRD, SDD or config text defines a per-ticket sub-folder.
why: AC-039 says "the feature's spec folder", and the config reader returns one `spec_folder`. If that value is already the feature folder, the document and GRILL-LOG.md land one level too deep, and to-prd (0008) must guess the same layout (unverified: the layout is undefined in every doc I read).
fix: Define the layout in one place (the config contract or the SDD) and make the grill and 0008 use it.
evidence: spec_dir = Path(config["spec_folder"]) / ticket_slug(args.ticket); read_config docstring "a non-empty folder path relative to the repository root"

criterion: Acceptance 1: the grill reads the ticket with its comments and links
finding: `adf_text` drops `mention`, `inlineCard`, `emoji` and `hardBreak` nodes without a mark, so a Jira comment loses the @name, the pasted ticket or URL link, and line breaks.
why: Tickets referenced by smart link in a body or comment are the links the grill is meant to read, and the loss is silent.
fix: Emit `attrs.text` for mention and emoji, `attrs.url` for inlineCard, and a newline for hardBreak.
evidence: text = adf_text(node.get("content")); return text.rstrip("\n") + "\n" if node.get("type") in BLOCK_NODES else text  (only `text` and `media*` are handled)

criterion: error and rollback paths: no JSON answer
finding: serve() does not catch OSError, so a file error gives a traceback and no JSON object.
why: On Windows os.replace in write_text raises PermissionError when another process (editor, antivirus, page host) holds the target. Path.read_text on the log, read_bytes on the raw file and Path.unlink are also unguarded. SKILL.md:21 promises one JSON object per command.
fix: Add OSError to the caught types and answer code 'io-error' with exit 2; retry os.replace a few times.
evidence: except (AttributeError, IndexError, KeyError, TypeError, ValueError) as error:

criterion: Mock echo / tautology: fake shaped to the code (engine)
finding: The fake invents the engine call shapes (poll answers `raw`, render answers `page`, `ingest DOC --raw-file F`, engine at `engine/engine.py`). The code reads exactly these, so every engine step passes by construction.
why: SDD §3 fixes only the verb names, the envelope and 'ingest also takes the raw response text', so a different real shape would still pass the dry runs. The only real-engine test runs `check` and is skipped until the engine merges.
fix: Mark these shapes as assumptions in the fake and add a real-engine round (present, poll, ingest) that replaces the fake once S1 merges; or take the shapes from ADR-0001 if it fixes them.
evidence: SDD §3 table: 'page document path; ingest also takes the raw response text'. fake_engine.py:158 `answer({"ok": True, "raw": raw})`, :160 `argv.index("--raw-file")`; test_grill.py:746-752 real engine runs only `check`.

criterion: Happy-path-only: ingest rules (acceptance: settles only what the §6 rules settle)
finding: Every dry run uses only `accept` and `note:` marks, in the fake's own grammar. No test sends `reopen`, `changes`, a write-in, two marks for one item, or a mark plus a note, and checks that the grill can only reopen, or settle by an existing note.
why: §6 sends these to needs_reading. `_settle` refuses a settle with no note (`no-note`), but nothing tests that for a needs_reading item that has no note.
fix: Add dry-run cases for `changes`, `reopen` and two-mark conflict that assert `needs_reading` has no notes, that `settle` is refused with `no-note`, and that `open` works.
evidence: fake_engine.py:10 'The raw response grammar here is the fake's own'; SDD §6 'reopen, changes and a write-in go to needs-reading. A conflict is 2 lines for one item.'

criterion: Mock echo / tautology: tracker fixtures
finding: The Jira issue-get fixture puts comments in `fields.comment.comments` and links in `fields.issuelinks`. The GitHub fixture has `comments[]` and an `issue-search` answer of `issues[{number}]`. The reader picks Jira or GitHub by testing for `fields` or `description_hash`. No source for these shapes exists in the repo.
why: SDD §3 and ADR-0003 name only the verbs. The fakes are called 'recorded' but nothing records where they came from, and acceptance bullet 1 passes on an invented shape.
fix: State in the fake's header the source of each answer shape (v1 client output, or the S3 contract file), or mark it unverified until the port merges.
evidence: read_ticket.py:43-44 `"fields" in answer or "description_hash" in answer`; grep of the repo for `description_hash` finds only read_ticket.py; SDD §3 sequence shows 'issue-get {key}' returning 'ok + description'.

criterion: Mock echo / tautology: missing-input refusal rests on the fake's error code
finding: The 'names the missing file and its writer' tests depend on the fake config reader answering code `no-config`. Any other refusal from the real reader reaches the human unchanged, without file and writer.
why: Acceptance bullet 6 (AC-003) is proven only against the fake's own error code. SDD says only 'one read command, JSON answer' for the config reader.
fix: Treat any refusal or non-JSON answer from the reader as missing-input, and test that; or pin the real code once S1 merges.
evidence: fake_config.py:17 `"code": "no-config"`; grill_start.py:30 `if refusal.code == "no-config"`; SDD §8 config reader 'one read command, JSON answer'.

criterion: Fragile / tautology: Codex branch (acceptance: on Codex it ends its turn and the Stop hook hands the answer back)
finding: The Codex dry run asserts that no `poll` is in the call log, but the test never runs `wait`, so the assertion cannot fail. The only other check is two substrings, 'End your turn' and 'Stop hook', in the Codex paragraph.
why: An edit that tells Codex to run the wait command would still pass.
fix: Assert that the Codex paragraph does not contain `step=wait` or the wait command text, and that the fenced wait block sits in the Claude branch only (the Claude half is already checked at :175-182).
evidence: test_grill.py:463 `assert world.verbs() == [..., "show", "ingest"]` with no wait call earlier in the test; :180-181 substring checks only.

criterion: Missing negative cases (mutation probe, sampled)
finding: Three mutants survive the ticket-reading tests. (1) `comments_cut` forced to 0. (2) The link cap `position >= MAX_LINKS` changed to `> MAX_LINKS + 100`. (3) The cross-repo `payload["tracker"]` line removed. No fixture has a total above the returned comments, more than 20 links, or a cross-repo link that is readable.
why: The comment-cut message and the over-limit message on the ticket card are untested, so a ticket with a long thread is read with no warning to the human.
fix: Add a fixture with `comment.total` greater than the comments returned and one with 21 links; assert `comments_cut`, the card text and the over-limit entry; make the cross-repo key resolvable and assert the payload.
evidence: Probe on a copy in C:/t/gmut, cases m10, m11, m12: all 4 ticket tests still pass. read_ticket.py:55, :117-119, :101-102.

criterion: Missing negative cases (mutation probe, sampled)
finding: Three mutants survive. (1) Removing the steer-target exclusion in `returning` (a steer on a map node must not return an older card). (2) Removing the 'returned and has no new card' failure from the gate. (3) `_live_notes` keeping deleted notes. The steer test puts the steer in round 1 on a current-round card, and no fixture has a deleted note.
why: A steer sent in a later round could reopen an old card, or a deleted note could be logged as an owner note, and every test would stay green.
fix: Add a round-2 steer test whose node belongs to a round-1 card (assert `returned == []`). Add a gate test for a returned card with no new card. Add a document with `deleted: true` and assert it is absent from the log.
evidence: Probe m14, m15, m9: 7, 3 and 11 selected tests pass. round_document.py:70 and :175, grill_log.py:213.

criterion: odd characters in row text
finding: Settled-row text built from a settle reading or a decided-card evidence/reverse text is not collapsed to one line.
why: A reading 'a\nb' gives '- Settled: T · settled by note R1 · reading: a' and a second line 'b · card i-1'. Neither line matches GENERATED. Both survive every sync as agent rows and a new pair is added each sync. Only _first_text is normalised.
fix: Apply ' '.join(value.split()) to reading, evidence and reverse before the row is built.
evidence: return f"settled by note R{settled['round']} · reading: {settled['reading']}"

criterion: odd characters in row text
finding: _split uses str.splitlines(), which also splits on U+0085, U+2028 and U+2029. json.dumps(ensure_ascii=False) leaves those characters raw in the Round 0 row and in owner-note lines.
why: A Round 0 text or a human note pasted with U+2028 is written as one line and read back as two blocks. The second fragment does not start with two spaces, so it becomes a stray agent row that sync never removes.
fix: Split on '\n' only (text.split('\n')) or write these JSON strings with ensure_ascii=True.
evidence: for line in rest[:end].splitlines():

criterion: gate admits a weaker status than the format
finding: STATUS_ROW accepts a bare 'unverified-external', with no '(human acknowledged)' citation.
why: A Ledger row '... → unverified-external' passes write_row and the exit gate. The format (GRILL-LOG-FORMAT.md:12) and the error text require a recorded acknowledgement.
fix: Require the form unverified-external \(.+\), like verified and refuted.
evidence: unverified-external\b.*)$")

criterion: resume after a crash at each step
finding: Once the gate row exists, start answers resume false with a new session, so a crash between step 9 and step 10 cannot reach Finish.
why: The gate passes, the process dies before the commit. The next start sees exit_gate_passed true and opens a fresh grill. The answer has no field that says the gate passed and the commit is pending.
fix: Add 'gate_passed: true' and the passed session to the start answer, and make step 1 say: go to step 10.
evidence: return None if exit_gate_passed(log, session) else session

criterion: resume after a crash at each step
finding: The clause 'or at step 3 when doc does not exist yet' sits under 'resume true', but resume is true only when a document exists. A crash after step 3 and before the first build gives resume false.
why: The log then holds Round 0 and Ledger rows, the session id is new, and the agent runs step 3 again and asks the human for round 0 a second time.
fix: Add 'log_has_rows' to the start answer, and tell the agent to read the log and skip step 3 when a Round 0 row exists.
evidence: resume = bool(resumed) ... return {... "resume": bool(resumed) ...} (grill_start.py:84-85)

criterion: resume after a crash at each step
finding: After a crash between ingest and apply-readings the raw file is gone, and no documented command lists what is still to read.
why: ingest deletes raw_file and the second ingest refuses with 'unreadable'. round_document.py has a 'pending' verb (line 380), but no step names it.
fix: Name 'round_document.py pending --doc' in step 1 for a resume with an answered current round.
evidence: Path(raw_file).unlink()  (page_round.py:52)

criterion: second session on one ticket
finding: There is no session lock. Two sessions on one ticket resume the same document and the same raw file.
why: Both read the document, change it and write it back, so the last write wins. Both write 'GRILL-LOG.md.tmp' and 'grill-<id>.json.tmp', so one os.replace can fail. Two fresh starts in the same second share one session id because the id is checked only against an existing document.
fix: Create an exclusive lock file per session and refuse a start while another live holder has it.
evidence: scratch = path.with_name(path.name + ".tmp")  (grill_common.py:55)

criterion: odd characters in a claim or term
finding: The row key is the text before the first ' → ', so two claims that contain the arrow share a key and the second overwrites the first.
why: 'Ledger: A → B → pending' and 'Ledger: A → C → verified (x)' both have key '- Ledger: A'. The first claim is lost without a message. The same applies to a Policy actor or a Spinoff summary that contains an arrow.
fix: Split on the last ' → <status>' with the STATUS_ROW pattern for Ledger and Term.
evidence: return f"- {kind}: {text.split(' → ')[0]}"

criterion: overwrite in place loses earlier input
finding: Devil is a single row that is overwritten, but ROUNDS.md:94 says 'Write a Devil row when each one is resolved'.
why: An agent that writes one row per finding keeps only the last finding. The gate passes on the existence of a row.
fix: Make the ROUNDS.md text say 'rewrite the one Devil row with every finding', or key Devil rows per finding.
evidence: SINGLE_KINDS = {"Round 0", "Examples", "Devil", "Escape"}

criterion: null or odd fields in a Jira answer
finding: adf_text drops hardBreak, mention, emoji and inlineCard nodes.
why: A Jira description line 'one<shift-enter>two' reads 'onetwo'. A mention or a smart link to another ticket is removed, so the human and the agent do not see the reference. Unverified: the ADF node types come from the Jira ADF spec, not from this tree.
fix: Emit '\n' for hardBreak, attrs.text for mention and emoji, and attrs.url for inlineCard.
evidence: if node.get("type") == "text": return node.get("text", "")

criterion: Acceptance 8 (PRD AC-043): a picture comes before a critical-aspect question
finding: The accepted picture roots include `map` and `freestyle`, which the visualize guide does not list as pictures of the current state, and the rule applies only when the agent sets `critical: true`.
why: A text-only freestyle root passes the check. Also, the guide says the picture goes "above the question", but a picture root with the question in `children` renders in the right order only if the engine draws a parent before its children (unverified: the engine is absent).
fix: Limit PICTURES to graph, table, sequence, run-strip, as the guide lists them.
evidence: PICTURES = {"map", "graph", "table", "sequence", "run-strip", "freestyle"}; visualize/SKILL.md: graph, table, sequence diagram, run-strip

criterion: Acceptance 6 (PRD AC-003): a missing input names the file and the skill that writes it
finding: Only `no-config` and a missing `tracker.kind` name `/afkv2:setup`; a config that exists without `spec_folder` re-raises the reader's `bad-value` refusal with no writer named.
why: That is also a required input the skill cannot run without, and AC-003 asks for the writer in every such stop.
fix: Map `bad-value` on `spec_folder` to `_missing(".afkv2/config.json spec_folder", SETUP)`.
evidence:
if refusal.code == "no-config": raise _missing(CONFIG, SETUP) from refusal
        raise

criterion: Wiring: every verb has a consumer
finding: The `pending` verb of the script has no step in SKILL.md and no test. Only the internal function is used.
why: A verb with no consumer is dead surface that can go stale.
fix: Remove the CLI verb, or add a step that uses it (for example a resume check).

finding: The page document location is checked only as `parent.name == 'pages'`. The test never asserts that it sits under `<spec_folder>/<ticket>/pages`.
why: A document written to any folder named `pages` would pass.

criterion: Obscure Test: refusal asserted through a harness assertion
finding: Refusals of `build` are tested with `pytest.raises(AssertionError, match=code)` on the harness's own returncode assertion text, instead of `expect=1` and reading `error.code`.
why: Any assertion error whose message contains the code string passes, and a wrong exit code is not distinguished.

evidence: test_grill.py:508, :514, :523, :540 `pytest.raises(AssertionError, match=...)`; World.run :77.

criterion: Vacuous negative: no step asks for a lane (acceptance, AC-004)
finding: The only check is the absence of the word 'lane' in `*.md`. A step that asks for a track, route or mode passes, and the scripts are not scanned.
why: The bullet is about behaviour (no step asks for or chooses one), not one word.
fix: Also scan the scripts and add the owner's synonyms, or state in the test that the word check is the accepted proxy.

criterion: Missing negative case: present refusals
finding: Only a `render` refusal is tested. A `check` refusal (stop before render) and a `show` refusal (the Markdown fallback path in SKILL.md step 5) are not tested.
why: The 'stops at the first refusal' rule is shown for one verb only.

criterion: open-question: all-or-nothing readings
finding: `apply_readings` says 'all or nothing', but each refusal test sends one entry. No payload has a valid entry followed by an invalid one to show that nothing is written.
why: A later refactor that writes per entry would pass every test.

criterion: a GitHub key in #7 or owner/name#7 form
finding: Link dedup and the issue-search query use the bare number from the tracker, but a reference in text can be 'owner/name#7' or '#7' for the same issue.
why: Ticket '7' read with 'owner/name#7' in a comment: the self-reference is read as a link, and 'owner/name#9' and '#9' are read twice. issue-search runs 'gh issue list', which lists open issues only and stops at 50 (verified in the s3 tracker port: github_issues.py issue_search, DEFAULT_LIMIT = 50). Closed mentions are missing and nothing reports it.
fix: Normalise keys to repo#number (repo from config) before dedup; pass state 'all' or report the cut.
evidence: links, seen = [], {issue["key"]}

criterion: Windows paths and encodings
finding: JSON reads use utf-8, not utf-8-sig.
why: A round input or readings file written by Windows PowerShell with a BOM is refused as 'unreadable'. A --text-file with a BOM puts U+FEFF into the row text, so the row key differs from the same claim without it (grill_log.py:261).
fix: Read with utf-8-sig in read_json and in the --text-file decode.
evidence: return json.loads(Path(path).read_text("utf-8"))

criterion: a missing or corrupt document
finding: One unreadable or malformed older grill document makes every sync fail.
why: sync reads every grill-*.json beside the current one. A corrupt old file gives 'unreadable' (or KeyError on doc["session"]), and the agent can only stop.
fix: Skip an unreadable older document and report it in the answer as 'skipped'.
evidence: docs += [read_json(path) for path in doc_path.parent.glob("grill-*.json") if path.resolve() != doc_path.resolve()]

criterion: a GitHub key in #7 or owner/name#7 form
finding: The spec folder name comes from the key as typed: '#7' gives '7' and 'owner/name#7' gives 'owner-name-7'.
why: The same issue invoked in two forms gets two spec folders and two GRILL-LOG.md files. Unverified: the folder rule of the later skills is not in this slice.
fix: Slug the bare issue number for GitHub keys, or store the key form in the start answer.

criterion: resume after a crash at each step
finding: raw_pending compares the file text with the stored 'raw' string. If the engine stores raw in another form, the same answer is ingested twice.
why: Crash after the engine ingest and before unlink: the raw file stays. A stored form that differs by a trailing newline or by line ends makes raw_pending true. Unverified: the real engine is not in this tree, so the stored form is not known.
fix: Compare after stripping line ends, or delete the raw file in a try/finally in the same step as ingest.
evidence: return raw not in stored
